record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: Suppose an egg O(n, 2n, q) contains a sub pseudo-conic, where the paper uses “pseudo-conic” for a regular pseudo-oval arising from a conic. Must the egg then be good?

evidence.quote: 8. Is an O(n, 2n, q) with a sub pseudo-conic always good?
A regular pseudo-oval for which O1 is a conic is called either a pseudo-conic or a classical pseudo-oval.

An egg O = O(n, 2n, q), respectively a TGQ T(O), is called good at an element π ∈ O if for every two distinct elements π and π′ of O − {π} the (3n − 1)-dimensional space < π, π′, π > contains exactly qn + 1 elements of O; in such a case π is called a good element of O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power and n a positive integer. An egg O(n, 2n, q) is a set E of q^{2n}+1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(4n−1, q) such that:
(i) any three of them span a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace, and
(ii) every element π ∈ E is contained in a unique (3n−1)-dimensional subspace τ(π), called the tangent space of E at π, that is disjoint from all other elements of E.

Such an egg E is said to be good at an element π ∈ E if for every two distinct elements π′, π″ of E ∖ {π}, the (3n−1)-dimensional space ⟨π, π′, π″⟩ contains exactly q^n + 1 elements of E; the egg E is called good if it is good at some element.

A pseudo-oval in PG(3n−1, q) is a set of q^n + 1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces, every three of which span PG(3n−1, q). A pseudo-oval is called regular if it arises by field reduction from an oval O₁ in PG(2, q^n); when O₁ can be taken to be a (nondegenerate) conic, the regular pseudo-oval is called a pseudo-conic.

A sub pseudo-conic of an egg O(n, 2n, q) is a subset of q^n + 1 of its elements that all lie in a common (3n−1)-dimensional subspace and form a pseudo-conic there.

Question: Must every egg O(n, 2n, q) that contains a sub pseudo-conic be good?
artifact.status_search_result: For q even, results of Brown and Lavrauw show that an egg O(n,2n,q) containing a pseudo-conic is classical (arising from an elliptic quadric), and classical eggs are good at every element; thus the answer is affirmative in even characteristic. For q odd, no general resolution of the question appears in the literature found, so the problem appears to remain open in the odd case.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-pointed conic
status_evidence.snippet: An egg in PG(4n−1,q), q even, contains a pseudo-conic if and only if the egg is classical (arising from an elliptic quadric in PG(3,q^n)).
status_evidence.claim: For q even, an egg containing a pseudo-conic is classical, hence good.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-conic
status_evidence.snippet: The egg O(n,2n,q) of PG(4n−1,q), q even, is classical if and only if O is good at some element and contains at least one pseudo-conic, or contains at least two intersecting pseudo-conics.
status_evidence.claim: Even-characteristic case is resolved by Brown–Lavrauw type results.
